hints: At each boundary, the net flow is constrained by the cumulative food surplus.
On a circle, one common offset can be added to every boundary flow.
Choose the offset minimizing the sum of absolute flows: a median.
analogy: A circulation around the table may be added without changing any child's final amount; choose the cheapest circulation.
example: For surpluses [2,-1,-1], prefix sums are [2,1,0]. Their median is 1, giving cost 1+0+1=2.
algorithm: For each child compute current food minus desired food and its cyclic prefix sum. Find a median of these n prefix sums and sum the absolute differences from it. Use a wide integer.
correctness: Flow conservation forces adjacent boundary flows to differ by each child's surplus, so all feasible flows are prefix sums shifted by a common constant. A median minimizes their total absolute value, and that value is the number of unit transfers.
complexity: For n children, O(n log n) time using sorting and O(n) space.
